papers.title: Rewired decoding fuels KRAS-driven cancer growth and drug resistance
papers.abstract: Dimethylation of the translation elongation factor eEF1A at lysine 55 by the dual methyltransferase METTL13 enhances decoding of a discrete set of low-frequency codons with weak wobble-position base pairing. This process selectively sustains synthesis of oncoproteins, including KRAS. METTL13 ablation restores sensitivity to inhibitors of the KRAS-G12C mutant and prolongs survival in models of lung adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: Cancer cells have got ‘MoVes’
papers.abstract: Motile vesicles (MoVes) are a previously undescribed population of large extracellular vesicles released from the trailing edge of actively migrating cancer cells. MoVes carry the entire genome and mutational landscape of the parental tumour cell, together with intracellular organelles, including mitochondria, and proteins associated with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and organelle biology.

papers.title: Twenty years of induced pluripotent stem cells
papers.abstract: In 2006, Shinya Yamanaka and Kazutoshi Takahashi used OCT4, SOX2, KLF4 and MYC (OSKM; also known as Yamanaka factors) to generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from somatic cells. Twenty years later, the field has made remarkable progress, both technically and in terms of its applications. To celebrate the twentieth anniversary of iPSCs, we asked experts around the globe about their view on the most striking achievements and next challenges to overcome.

papers.title: Microtubule lattice state regulates Rho GTPase
papers.abstract: Taxanes are effective anti-cancer microtubule (MT) drugs, yet why they clinically outperform other spindle poisons is unclear. New work shows that taxanes, unlike other MT-stabilizing agents, force MT lattices into an expanded state that evicts GEF-H1, coupling MT pharmacology to Rho signalling and actin remodelling in interphase.

papers.title: Turning a Staphylococcus aureus virulence factor into an antibacterial therapy
papers.abstract: We describe FibriLysins, dual-action proteins that dismantle the fibrin structures encapsulating Staphylococcus aureus multicellular communities and kill the bacteria within. In a mouse model of device-associated infection, FibriLysins demonstrate higher antibacterial efficacy compared with the standard-of-care antibiotic vancomycin. These findings highlight the potential of FibriLysins to treat recalcitrant S. aureus infections.

papers.title: Systemic Analysis of Patient Derived Esophageal Epithelial Organoid Model Reveals Cell State Heterogeneity and Conservation of Differentiation Hierarchy
papers.abstract: Background and Aims: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) features prominent epithelial dysregulation that persists despite resolution of eosinophilia. Interleukin-13 (IL-13) is known to be a key upstream driver of epithelial abnormalities in EoE. We sought to benchmark an IL-13 esophageal organoid model against the in vivo epithelial state in EoE at a single cell resolution, to define in the role of IL-13 in aberrant epithelial development and inflammation in EoE, and to validate the IL-13 organoid as a model system to study the epithelial changes seen in EoE. Methods: We performed scRNA-Seq on esophageal biopsies from control and EoE patients, and esophageal biopsy-derived organoids with or without IL-13. We compared cellular composition, differentiation trajectories, pathway enrichment, and differential gene expression within both systems, and assessed findings at a protein level. Results: Seven distinct epithelial cell clusters were identified and preserved in both biopsies and organoids. EoE biopsies demonstrated expansion of cycling cells, whereas IL-13-treated organoids showed shift in the composition of the suprabasal compartments. Pseudotime topology was preserved across tissues, with a shift away from terminal differentiation in both EoE biopsies and IL-13-treated organoids. IL-13 reproduced changes in the transcription of central EoE genes and the dysregulation of epithelial proliferation and differentiation pathways seen in EoE. There was broad activation of immune related pathways within both EoE biopsies and IL-13-treated organoids, however, biopsies additionally showed activation in several immune and extracellular matrix remodeling programs that IL-13 alone did not reproduce. Conclusion: IL-13-treated esophageal organoids replicate key epithelial features of EoE including dysregulated epithelial development, impaired cornification, and inflammatory signals, while preserving lineage architecture, providing a tractable platform for epithelial-targeted mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

papers.title: Dysplastic Alveolar Basaloid Cells Provide a Protective Barrier via KRT17-Stratifin Complex during Chronic Fibrosis
papers.abstract: Understanding how lung alveolar type 2 (AT2) stem cells respond to chronic profibrotic insults in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is critical for developing therapies and determining physiological relevance of maladaptive regeneration. Using integrated snATAC/snRNA-sequencing of human lungs and in vitro models, we mapped distinct AT2 regenerative trajectories: resolvable euplastic repair and persistent dysplastic repair. Spatially restricted ITGB6/TGF{beta}1/SMAD3 signaling drives AT2-to-basaloid dysplasia via direct upregulation of KRT17 and Stratifin. Using murine models of dysplastic repair and a human precision-cut lung slice/stem cell incorporation assay, we show that KRT17 and its interaction with Stratifin are required for AT2 cell flattening, alveolar coverage, and barrier protection. AT2s leverage these mechanisms to re-epithelialize damaged tissue during chronic fibrosis, navigating a delicate balance between preventing further lung damage and driving aberrant epithelial remodeling. Collectively, we identify novel mechanisms governing alveolar metaplasia and its functional relevance, offering crucial insights for therapeutic interventions in fibrotic lung diseases.

papers.title: A Transcriptionally Distinct Intermediate Activation State Precedes Langerhans Cell Migration from the Epidermis
papers.abstract: Langerhans cells (LC) are antigen-presenting cells that form dense epidermal networks for immune surveillance. Upon antigen uptake, LCs are activated and subsequently orchestrate immune responses by migrating into the lymphatic system. However, the regulation of transcriptional programs during activation and the behavior of LCs in vivo during this transition remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study combines single-cell transcriptomic analysis with intravital imaging to reconstruct the activation trajectory of epidermal LCs. In particular, the study generates a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic dataset comprising over 22,000 high-quality epidermal LCs under both homeostatic and injury conditions. Notably, a distinct intermediate activated state that precedes LC migration was identified and characterized at the level of signaling pathways and transcription factors. The integration of this dataset with external datasets from homeostatic and injured skin reveals wound-specific fibroblasts as the major source of C3, which is the central component of the complement cascade. Moreover, intravital imaging of C3-deficient mice and pegcetacoplan treatment demonstrates that C3 contributes to LC accumulation adjacent to wound sites. Collectively, the study findings identify an activated epidermal LC population and implicate complement signaling in the regulation of LC behavior during skin injury.

papers.title: Molecule-resolved inference reveals the spatial organization of transcriptional programs
papers.abstract: Transcriptional programs encode cellular identity and physiological activity, linking gene regulation to cellular phenotypes. Although spatial transcriptomics measures individual RNA molecules across intact tissues, most analyses aggregate them into cells or pixels, obscuring molecular level functional dynamics. We introduce FICTURE2, a statistical model that infers the transcriptional program from which each individual molecule is generated, using gene identity and spatial context alone without segmentation or binning. FICTURE2 learns programs with distinct spatial distributions, ranging from millimeter-scale continuous transition to micron-scale subcellular localization, the coexisting patterns of which then reveal both cellular identity and physiological activity with unified interpretations. FICTURE2 supports both unsupervised and reference-guided inference and is orders of magnitude more efficient than alternative approaches, enabling systematic analysis of large-scale spatial datasets as we demonstrate in data across diverse tissue types profiled by various spatial technologies.

papers.title: An invariant network architecture with broadly expressed regulators distinguishes cell-type from cell-state identity in situ
papers.abstract: Core regulatory networks (CRNs) of tissue-specific master transcription factors (TFs) are essential for defining cell identity and are widely used to reprogram cells and to decipher pathogenic mechanisms. However, to date, CRNs have only been described at the cell-type level: their characteristics in the distinct states that a single cell type can adopt have not been examined. This leaves open what the cell-type CRNs actually represent. Here, using the zonated hepatocyte states of the mouse liver as a model system, we construct the first state-level CRNs in a native tissue. For this purpose, we developed a robust LCM-Spatial-ATAC-seq method that achieves bulk-level data quality from microdissected cell populations. By identifying what is shared among the state-level CRNs, we determined what is cell-type defining: an invariant sub-network of core-regulatory TFs (crTFs) that maintains identical positions and conserved interactions in the CRNs. Unexpectedly, the top positions of this invariant sub-network are occupied by broadly expressed TFs rather than the well-established master TFs, which reside downstream. Yet the state-level CRNs are clearly different, both in terms of composition and interactions. The former are dominated by zone-specific regulators, whereas the latter are spread throughout the network, encompassing about one third of all interactions between the states. Thus, our results reveal a novel dual character of a cell's CRN: an invariant sub-network that defines the cell-type identity, together with a variable peripheral network that underlies its state specialization.

papers.title: Digital twins forecast individual immune trajectories
papers.abstract: The human immune system differs markedly between individuals and changes in response to infection, vaccination and treatment. AI virtual cells are being built to simulate cellular responses to perturbation. Yet these models, like most immune-response predictors, describe each person by a single pre-challenge measurement and forecast change from patterns pooled across people. Digital twins, updated with every new observation of an individual, could forecast how that person's immune state changes. Here we present ImmuneTwins, which builds these twins from single-cell profiles by personalizing a shared virtual-cell model with each individual's observations. In two external populations, ImmuneTwins reduced immune-age error by 32% and 42% relative to the best existing method. During repeated influenza vaccination, its twins predicted the direction of immune-cell change 35% more accurately than the best published method, and their error fell by 27% as observations accumulated. The twins revealed that immune cells and plasma proteins recover about half their deviation from a persistent personal reference within 90 days, whereas response size varies between challenges. They further localized B-cell remodelling in exceptional longevity and anticipated patient-specific immune trajectories during myeloma treatment. These results establish virtual-cell digital twins for forecasting individual immune change and identifying each person's characteristic immune features.

papers.title: flashscenic: Accelerated GRN Analysis with RegDiffusion for Large-Scale Single-Cell Data
papers.abstract: Single-cell gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis via the SCENIC framework provides biologically interpretable cell-state representations through motif-validated transcription factor (TF) regulon activities. However, sequential, CPU-bound implementations (pySCENIC) constrain scalability to highly variable genes and make the repeated executions needed to resolve network stochasticity computationally prohibitive. Furthermore, while regulon activity is hypothesized to mitigate technical batch effects, its integration performance has never been quantitatively assessed against modern data integration benchmarks. We present flashscenic, an end-to-end GPU-accelerated framework that resolves these bottlenecks and expands the practical scope of single-cell regulatory genomics. By reformulating module construction, cisTarget motif pruning, and AUCell scoring into batched GPU tensor operations, flashscenic achieves a 12- to 27-fold downstream speedup over pySCENIC, while maintaining strict numerical equivalence (Pearson r = 0.9996). Leveraging this throughput, we conducted the first systematic benchmark of nine consensus aggregation strategies across multiple independent tissue cohorts, demonstrating that discrete post-pruning recurrence voting ([≥]50% recurrence, [≥]5 targets per regulon) maximizes biological fidelity. Finally, data integration benchmarking across a 116,043-cell acute myeloid leukemia (AML) atlas quantitatively demonstrates that uncorrected TF activity provides an intrinsic, unsupervised batch-integration benefit over raw PCA. Combining it with a standard batch integration method matches or outperforms canonical expression-based integration while accurately recovering lineage-defining and oncogenic regulators (CEBPA, HOXA9). flashscenic is available via pip install flashscenic, with source code and tutorials at https://github.com/haozhu233/flashscenic.

papers.title: PatHoST: weakly supervised reconstruction of pathogen spatial distributions from host transcriptomes
papers.abstract: Dual host-pathogen spatial transcriptomics enables spatially resolved investigation of infection, yet the completeness of pathogen detection remains poorly characterized. Here, we generated pathogen-only spatial transcriptomic sections from a chronic Mycobacterium abscessus lung infection model to experimentally benchmark pathogen detection, revealing substantially increased pathogen transcript recovery compared with conventional dual profiling. Building on these data, we developed PatHoST, a weakly supervised computational framework that uses pathogen-derived information to generate silver-standard labels and learns host transcriptional programs predictive of pathogen presence. PatHoST reconstructed pathogen spatial distributions across independent tissue sections and enabled the identification of localized host regulatory programs beyond conventional cluster-based analyses. Application to human SARS-CoV-2 lung spatial transcriptomics supported generalization across host species and pathogen classes. Together, PatHoST combines purpose-built experimental benchmarking with weakly supervised inference to recover latent pathogen information and extend the analytical capabilities of dual host-pathogen spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Kontext: Kernel-based method bridging spatial domain identification and cell-cell communication
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of biological tissues is characterized by spatial domains: regions with coherent transcriptional and anatomical properties, heavily influenced by local cell-cell interactions. Although identifying spatial domains is a common task in spatial transcriptomics, most existing methods provide limited mechanistic insight into their organization. We present Kontext, a kernel-based framework that jointly represents cells and their local environments, enabling the identification of spatial domains grounded in their underlying ligand-receptor interactions. This representation further provides complementary outputs for characterizing cellular microenvironments, spatial niches, and sender-receiver communication patterns. Kontext outperforms state-of-the-art methods in recovering reference domain annotations across several spatial transcriptomics technologies and biological models, while offering improved computational efficiency and scalability. Applying Kontext on a Xenium temporal mouse heart cryoinjury dataset, we characterize the spatiotemporal evolution of the injury and identify an undescribed sustained activity of the complement system in the communication between fibroblasts and macrophages during scar maturation. In a million-cell three-dimensional Open-ST dataset of human metastatic lymph node tissue, we combine spatial domain identification and niche analysis to define the boundary region between the tumor and its microenvironment, revealing distinct communication patterns between this interface and the tumor core.

papers.title: Mechanistic gene-regulation-based trajectory inference with bowside
papers.abstract: While single-cell RNA sequencing enables the in-depth study of differentiation processes, simultaneous trajectory inference and gene regulatory network reconstruction remain challenging. We propose bowside, a shallow neural stochastic differentiation model that mechanistically models gene regulation. Our method successfully recovers gene expression trends and the underlying regulatory interactions. We demonstrate bowside on hematopoiesis and induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming data, retrieving known fate-determining network motifs.

papers.title: smoothclust: Spatial smoothing and boundary-density summaries for spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the measurement of gene expression while preserving tissue organization. A common analysis task is the identification of spatial domains, defined here as spatially coherent regions with consistent expression profiles or cell-type mixtures and represented using categorical spatial tissue maps. However, while numerous methods have been developed to identify spatial domains, interpretable summary measures to quantify spatial domain organization and tissue architecture at the sample level remain less standardized. Here, we present smoothclust, a framework for spatial domain analysis consisting of two components: a spatial-smoothing-based clustering workflow for generating spatial domain labels, and a boundary density (BD) metric that provides local and sample-level summaries of label transitions on a spatial graph. Building on established categorical spatial statistics, the raw BD metric is calculated from the proportion of neighboring spatial locations that are assigned to different domain labels, and requires only spatial coordinates and domain labels as inputs. The metric can be calculated using either our spatial-smoothing-based domain labels or labels from external clustering methods or manual annotations. Relative BD is a composition-adjusted summary, calculated by dividing raw BD by its expectation under random relabeling with the observed label counts. By quantifying label transitions, our framework translates spatial domain label maps into interpretable local and sample-level summary measures of tissue architecture, facilitating exploratory analyses and comparisons across samples and biological conditions. We demonstrate the approach through evaluations across datasets from several spatial transcriptomics platforms and simulations. The spatial-smoothing workflow and BD metric are implemented in the smoothclust R package, which is freely available from Bioconductor and GitHub.

papers.title: Mantpy: a framework for extracellular matrix analysis in spatial proteomics
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics technologies now profile cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) together in situ. Yet analysis tools remain cell-centric, despite the ECM playing an essential role in health and disease. Here we present Mantpy, a framework that represents the ECM, and its interface with cells, as spatial graphs. Mantpy builds ECM graphs directly from matrix markers and links them with cell graphs for joint cell-ECM analysis, supporting graph statistics, explainable graph deep learning and visualisation. Mantpy extends from a single ECM marker to multiplexed cell-ECM panels. It recovers layered tissue architecture in the intestine from collagen IV alone, quantifies infection-associated ECM remodelling in mouse liver, and relates cells to the surrounding matrix in mouse lung, where cellular context recovers synthetically corrupted matrix labels. Released with ECM-inclusive datasets and interoperating with the scverse ecosystem and pytorch geometric.

papers.title: Evolution of immune infiltration and immune triad formation across early melanoma progression
papers.abstract: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) in melanoma are a clinically important prognostic marker and are routinely used to inform patient care. However, when immune recognition of transformed melanocytes begins and how it evolves during early melanoma progression is not well understood. Using spatial transcriptomics and a unique cohort of patient-matched lesions representing multiple stages of early evolution, we investigate T cells, dendritic cells (DCs) and multi-cell immune "triads" during melanoma initiation. We find that T cell and DC density, triad density, and triad proximity to melanoma cells are elevated in regions of Stage I invasive melanoma as compared to Stage 0 in situ lesions and nevi. Further, we find that triad abundance correlates with both T cell and DC density, but is not predicted by clustering patterns of these cell types over larger spatial scales. We conclude that immune recognition of melanoma and engagement with the lesion significantly increases with progression from Stage 0 to Stage I disease. Further, using nevi that are depth-matched in the dermis to Stage I invasive lesions, we demonstrate this increased immune recognition is not a consequence of dermal invasion alone. This points to a paradigm where immune engagement of invasive melanoma reflects recognition of melanoma cell-intrinsic changes that emerge in Stage I disease.

papers.title: Anatomically matched spatial comparisons identify Trps1 as a regulator of knee interzone formation
papers.abstract: How the interzone forms and gives rise to articular cartilage, ligaments, and synovium is incompletely understood. Using our previously generated spatial and single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the mouse hindlimb, we compared the knee interzone with neighboring tissues and with the ankle interzone at matched positions, and identified Trps1 as a knee interzone-enriched candidate. Pseudotime analysis placed Trps1-high cells in a transitional state between chondrogenic progenitors and matrix-producing chondrocytes, with higher chondrogenic and lower fibroblastic program scores. Targeted Trps1 knockdown in hindlimb explants disrupted joint formation, permitted Col2a1 expression within the interzone, and reduced adjacent cartilage formation. The associated chondrogenic program was conserved in the human embryonic knee, whereas TRPS1 expression in osteoarthritic cartilage was associated with a fibroblastic matrix program. These results support a role for Trps1 in knee interzone development and show that anatomically matched spatial comparison with explant perturbation can nominate and test joint regulators.

papers.title: Regionalisation of muscle nucleus heterogeneity in foetal skeletal muscle
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle is organized into functional domains with attachments at both extremities to tendons via the myotendinous junction (MTJ) and innervation in the middle via the neuromuscular junction (NMJ). In adult muscle, the molecular heterogeneity of muscle domains is described at the level of myonuclei with specialized MTJ and NMJ myonuclei at the tips and middle of muscle fibre. However, how molecular heterogeneity emerges during development remains poorly understood. Combining single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing approaches with in situ hybridization experiments to limb muscles of chicken embryos, we uncover transcriptionally distinct muscle nuclei according to tip and central domains, both in myofibres and in mononucleated myogenic cells. At early foetal stage, all myonuclei display either a tip or a central domain identity. Immature mononucleated myogenic cells are enriched in the tip domain. Tip myonuclei of foetal muscles show a robust transcriptional signal transduction signature, which highlights molecular crosstalks between tip myonuclei and adjacent tendon fibroblasts but also with the adjacent immature mononucleated myogenic cells. We propose that the tip muscle domain is a signalling centre interacting with tendon fibroblasts to regulate muscle/tendon attachment and with adjacent mononucleated muscle cells to regulate myogenesis in limb foetal muscles.

papers.title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue–compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue–adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition–associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8 + T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.
papers.titleZh: Decoder-FFPE-seq：實現具備高靈敏度與單細胞解析度的基因體規模存檔組織空間轉錄體學
papers.summaryZh: 本研究介紹了一種名為 Decoder-FFPE-seq 的方法，透過結合 RNA 轉 DNA 探針轉換與墨印輔助條碼編碼技術，適用於福馬林固定石蠟包埋（FFPE）組織的空間 RNA 定序。該技術在小鼠大腦與存檔人類樣品的全身轉錄體分析中，相較於現有平台展現了超過 2.6 倍的靈敏度提升，並具備單細胞解析度。它能解析低豐度基因的細胞身份、更細緻的組織結構，並捕獲具預後價值的上皮間質轉化相關特徵。此外，Decoder-FFPE-seq 還能捕獲長鏈非編碼 RNA 與病毒 RNA，揭示其在口腔鱗狀細胞癌中的空間共調控網路，並在療程隊列中識別出可能與治療反應相關的 CD8+ T 細胞亞群。這項技術為基礎與轉譯研究中的存檔組織提供了強健、高解析度且易於使用的空間轉錄體學分析框架。

papers.title: Graph-based pangenome analysis uncovers structural and functional impacts of allopolyploidization events
papers.abstract: The emergence of graph pangenomes has advanced the study of structural variants (SVs) across diverse species, yet the impact of complex ploidy on SV landscapes remains poorly explored. Brettanomyces bruxellensis , a yeast shaped by multiple allopolyploidization events, offers a compelling model due to its well-characterized genomic and phenotypic diversity. Here, we integrated subgenome-resolved assemblies with population-scale genomic and transcriptomic datasets to characterize SV distribution and functional impact at the species level. Leveraging a reference graph pangenome, we detected 5972 unique SVs across 1060 isolates. Allopolyploid genomes harbored significantly more SVs (320 on average) than diploids (116), reflecting hybridization’s extensive impact on genome architecture. Functional association analysis revealed that 27.5% of SVs locally influence gene expression. Furthermore, a subset of SVs originating from ancestral divergence between subgenomes (hybridization-associated SVs) formed hotspots of structural diversity and disproportionately affect gene expression, with larger effect sizes than other SVs. These findings underscore allopolyploidization as a driver of structural and functional genomic diversification, highlighting the value of graph-based approaches in dissecting complex genome evolution.
papers.titleZh: 圖譜基礎泛基因組分析揭示異源多倍化事件的結構與功能影響

papers.title: A nematic framework for sprouting angiogenesis
papers.abstract: Sprouting angiogenesis is critical for embryogenesis, wound healing, and tumor growth. Here, we show that the liquid crystal framework, which has recently been leveraged to study various morphogenetic events, provides unique insight into angiogenic sprouting. In response to vascular endothelial growth factor, a potent proangiogenic factor, endothelial cells cultured on the surfaces of soft collagen hydrogels form elongated cell streams that coexist with more polygonal cell regions. Angiogenic sprouting initiates preferentially at cell stream tips, where nematic order gradients are most pronounced. We demonstrate that cell streams are associated with large traction forces that lead to three-dimensional deformations of the underlying hydrogel and that stream formation results from a delicate balance between microtubule polymerization and actomyosin contractility. Last, we show that active control of nematic order allows modulation of sprout formation, highlighting the key role of endothelial cell orientation gradients in angiogenic sprouting and paving the way for new therapeutic avenues.
papers.titleZh: 液晶框架解析血管新生芽生
papers.summaryZh: 本研究指出液晶框架能為血管新生芽生提供獨特見解。血管新生芽生對胚胎發生、傷口癒合與腫瘤生長至關重要。在血管內皮生長因子刺激下，培養於軟性膠原水凝膠表面的內皮細胞形成細長的細胞流，並與較多邊形的細胞區域共存。芽生傾向於在細胞流尖端啟動，該處向列有序梯度最明顯。研究顯示細胞流與較大的牽引力相關，導致基底水凝膠產生三維變形，且流的形成源於微管聚合與肌動蛋白-肌球蛋白收縮力之間的微妙平衡。此外，主動調控向列有序可調節芽生形成，凸顯內皮細胞取向梯度在血管新生芽生中的關鍵作用，並為新的治療途徑提供方向。

papers.title: Robust pan-junctional reinforcement preserves the gut epithelial barrier under mechanical stress
papers.abstract: Epithelia are specialized tissue barriers that safeguard the organism’s internal milieu from the external environment, a function critically dependent on intercellular junctions. In the colon, this barrier is repeatedly challenged by mechanical distension from feces, but it is unknown whether and how the colon adapts to this stress, which could otherwise compromise barrier integrity. Here, we show that feces-mediated mechanical distension triggers coordinated remodeling at cell and tissue scales, consistent with a mechanoadaptative response. This response includes recruitment of junctional proteins at all three types of adhesive cell-cell junctions (tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes). We identified protein-specific temporal profiles of junctional enrichment during distension, with ZO-1, E-cadherin, desmocollin 2, and plakoglobin exhibiting sustained junctional enrichment, whereas desmoplakin and keratin 8 showed progressive accumulation peaking at 15 min of distension. Distension was also accompanied by perijunctional recruitment and activation of nonmuscle myosin II (NMMII). Through genetic, pharmacological, and mechanical perturbations, we demonstrated that NMMII activation is required for epithelial mechanoadaptation. This process depends on extracellular calcium availability and mechanosensitive ion channel activity, supporting a role for calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling in NMMII-mediated junctional reinforcement. Loss of NMMII function impaired the junctional response to distension across all three junctional complexes, including desmosomes, resulting in disorganized junctions and barrier breach. Together, our findings uncover a robust physiological mechano-adaptive response of the adult colonic epithelium to an extrinsic mechanical stress, whereby coordinated reinforcement of all junctional complexes, requiring myosin II activity and calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling, preserves intestinal barrier integrity.
papers.titleZh: 強健的泛連接強化在機械壓力下維持腸道上皮屏障

papers.title: RNA binding by ADARs prevents RNA interference from attacking self-produced dsRNA
papers.abstract: The ability of an organism to distinguish between self and foreign double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is central to eliciting an immune response when needed while preventing autoimmunity. Using Caenorhabditis elegans , we investigated the interplay between two host pathways that regulate dsRNA expression and function, adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing by adenosine deaminases that act on RNA (ADARs), and RNA interference (RNAi). We found that the number of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) targeting edited genes is significantly up-regulated in ADAR mutant animals. In addition, despite an almost complete depletion of primary siRNAs generated from editing sites in wild-type animals, secondary siRNAs are generated from edited transcripts, suggesting that ADARs antagonize only the first step of RNAi processing. We show that ADARs interfere with the efficacy of exogenous RNAi in vivo, likely to prevent trans-silencing, and provide evidence that ADR-2 binding to dsRNA is required for efficient RNAi suppression. This work sheds light on how RNA editing safeguards self-dsRNAs against immune recognition and by-product degradation.
papers.titleZh: ADARs 結合 RNA 防止 RNA 干擾攻擊自身產生的 dsRNA

papers.title: Evidence of active whole-genome doubling (WGD) subclones in non-WGD tumors
papers.abstract: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) occurs frequently in human cancer and influences tumor evolution, metastasis, and treatment response. Here, we integrate bulk, single-cell, and spatial data to dissect the subclonal dynamics of WGD. Single-cell data analysis shows that WGD cells are prevalent even in tumors that are classified as non-WGD (nWGD). WGD subclones actively acquire somatic copy number alterations as they expand, suggesting ongoing evolution. We developed and rigorously validated a gene expression–based method, WAGES, to map WGD cell clonal fraction in bulk tumors. Applying WAGES to nWGD tumors, we reveal genomic correlates including TP53 mutations and chromosomal instability that are consistent with the presence of WGD subclones. Clinically, WAGES scores are strongly correlated with tumor metastatic potential, response to treatments including chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and patient prognosis. These findings reveal widespread WGD subclones in nWGD tumors and demonstrate their substantial impact on cancer evolution and therapeutic outcomes.
papers.titleZh: 非 WGD 腫瘤中存在活躍全基因組加倍亞克隆的證據

papers.title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its “microelectrode–drug reservoir–nanopore” configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction therapy.
papers.titleZh: 糖尿病性勃起功能障礙的軟性無線生物電子貼片
papers.summaryZh: 研究指出糖尿病引起的勃起功能障礙難以逆轉，主因是海綿體微環境長期受損，而傳統口服或海綿體內注射療法存在靶向性差、藥物分布不均及潛在併發症等問題。作者提出一種名為 SWEED 的軟性無線電子貼片，用於糖尿病性勃起功能障礙，宣稱可安全、非侵入且可控地調節陰莖微環境。該裝置採「微電極–藥物儲槽–奈米孔」配置，據稱能在奈米尺度強化局部電場並實現均勻經皮給藥。透過局部增強前列腺素 E1 的遞送，SWEED 在體外與體內實驗中顯示促進血管因子表現、改善海綿體血流灌注，並達到與臨床海綿體內注射療法相當的血管再生與功能恢復。此外，研究指出其可活化促勃起訊息路徑 EP2/PKA/CREB，並抑制 TGF-β/Smad 路徑，顯著減輕海綿體纖維化。

papers.title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
papers.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.
papers.titleZh: 人類帶毛髮皮膚類器官揭示 HSV-1 感染的細胞類型特異性易感性與先天免疫反應
papers.summaryZh: 研究使用人類帶毛髮皮膚類器官，並結合單細胞空間轉錄組學與影像，描繪 HSV-1 在皮膚結構中的擴散與宿主反應。數據顯示 HSV-1 生活史在表皮角質細胞與毛囊細胞中的進展，相較於真皮為延遲。感染誘發空間性宿主反應，包括乳頭層纖維母細胞中 IER3 的誘導。基底角質細胞中 IRF3 在感染細胞與鄰近未感染細胞皆上升，符合旁分泌抗病毒訊號活化。發炎反應以細胞類型特異方式區隔，乳頭層纖維母細胞誘導 TNFSF9 (4-1BBL)，角質細胞誘導腫瘤壞死因子-α (TNF-α)，ELISA 確認這些細胞因子及 TNF-α 應答性趨化因子 CXCL2 與 CXCL10 的分泌。研究指出 interferon-β 可降低病毒複製，而 TNF-α 與 4-1BBL 則無此效果，暗示其主要角色為協調免疫細胞招募與活化。

papers.title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3
papers.abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against “unseen” epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.
papers.titleZh: 利用 AlphaFold 3 從序列一般預測 T 細胞受體抗原特異性

papers.title: Intrinsic cellular persistent firing sustains hippocampal spatial representations during working memory
papers.abstract: Neurons are the fundamental units of cognitive processing. The prevailing view holds that neurons are input-output units that fire action potentials only upon receiving sufficient synaptic input. Here, we demonstrate that this may not be the sole operational mode of neurons in vivo during cognitive tasks, by showing that hippocampal place cells actively maintain firing and preserve spatial information through molecularly defined intrinsic mechanisms. Using in vitro and in vivo recordings coupled with molecular manipulation in mice, we reveal that hippocampal persistent firing during spatial working memory is supported by individual neurons via TRPC4 ion channels. Despite the general belief that persistent activity maintains working memory content, we demonstrate that persistent firing instead maintains immediate spatial representations, potentially supporting the encoding of spatial information to guide behavior. These findings position individual neurons as active contributors to information retention, extending their traditional role as passive input-output units and potentially broadening our understanding of neural computation.

papers.title: LAMP2A gene therapy mitigates Parkinson’s disease–related pathology in nonhuman primates
papers.abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson’s disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

papers.title: PDS5A and TOP2B cooperate for chromatin recruitment via CTCF
papers.abstract: PDS5A, a cohesin regulatory subunit, and topoisomerase IIB (TOP2B), an enzyme resolving DNA topological problems, interact with CTCF and regulate transcription and genome organization. We ascertained that PDS5A and TOP2B are recruited to CTCF-bound chromatin cooperatively and that catalytically active TOP2B increases PDS5A occupancy genome wide. Notably, the amino-terminal 95 to 116 amino acids of CTCF interacts with PDS5A, giving rise to CTCF-PDS5A-TOP2B interaction in vitro and to PDS5A chromatin enrichment via active TOP2B in vivo. PDS5A-TOP2B function together in moderating the resultant gene expression and genome organization. Loss of CTCF (95 to 116 amino acids) led to dysregulated gene expression and mildly reduced chromatin loops. In gliomas, PDS5A and TOP2B expression levels vary, but correlate, contributing to distinctive gene expression patterns. Inducible PDS5A knockdown led to reduced TOP2B occupancy and altered gene expression. Furthermore, PDS5A mediated sensitivity to TOP2 cancer drugs in glioma cells. This functional interaction between PDS5A and TOP2B at CTCF boundaries expands upon the mechanisms affecting gene regulation through genome organization, with implications for glioma therapeutics.
papers.titleZh: PDS5A 與 TOP2B 透過 CTCF 合作進行染色質招募

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure of a protein nanopore reveals lipid acyl chains as integral components
papers.abstract: Nanopore-based technologies are revolutionizing nucleic acid sequencing and molecular sensing, yet the structural basis by which pore-forming proteins interact with lipid membranes remains poorly defined. The mycobacterial porin MspA is a benchmark biological nanopore owing to its exceptional stability and uniquely narrow constriction, but accurate structural information is limited to protein-only models. Here, we present a 2.5-angstrom resolution cryo–electron microscopy structure of the M2 mutant of MspA embedded in a phospholipid nanodisc, providing a high-resolution experimental observation of MspA in a lipid environment. The structure reveals an annular arrangement of extended lipid acyl chains surrounding the MspA oligomer and contacting the transmembrane barrel. Their resolved densities indicate a substantially more ordered annular lipid environment than would be expected from a largely heterogeneous and nonspecific protein-lipid interface. The structure also demonstrates how specific M2 MspA mutations modulate pore polarity, influencing ion selectivity and transport. By determining the membrane-embedded structure of MspA and revealing an ordered arrangement of acyl chains forming extensive hydrophobic interactions with the protein, this study demonstrates the importance of the surrounding lipid environment in the design of protein nanopores.
papers.titleZh: 冷凍電子顯微鏡解析蛋白質奈米孔結構揭示脂質醯基鏈為其組成成分

papers.title: Mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by a glutamine antagonist radioenhancer conjugate drives pyroptosis and antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo- l -norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti–PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.
papers.titleZh: 穀氨酰胺拮抗劑放射增敏劑偶聯物誘導粒線體代謝重編程驅動焦亡與抗腫瘤免疫

papers.title: Integrative discovery and functional dependency mapping uncover essential chimeric RNAs in the active transcriptome
papers.abstract: Chimeric RNAs are a class of molecules defined as RNA transcripts containing genetic information for multiple genes. While their expression patterns across tissue types and disease states have been well documented, the biological function of these transcripts remains poorly understood. In this study, we developed an integrative prediction pipeline to establish an atlas of 569,640 chimeric RNAs across 1019 cancer cell lines. Leveraging this resource, we performed a systematic functional dependency screen by integrating our predictions with perturbation datasets from The Cancer Dependency Map project. This approach moves beyond prediction to identifying high-confidence functional chimeric RNAs essential for cellular processes, including a subset of recurrent chimeric transcripts generated by cis - splicing of adjacent genes. We demonstrate that depletion of selected candidate chimeras disrupts cell cycle progression and cellular fitness and that these transcripts are frequently dysregulated in primary breast tumors. Together, these results demonstrate that chimeric RNAs constitute a previously underappreciated layer of gene expression, expanding the functional genome beyond conventional genetics.
papers.titleZh: 整合性發現與功能依賴性圖譜揭示活躍轉錄組中必需的嵌合RNA

papers.title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB repairs diabetic neuropathy
papers.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) affects up to half of people with diabetes and lacks disease-modifying therapy. Here, we profiled MSC-EV biodistribution and multiomic programs across diabetic models, with key nerve repair established in db/db mice and corroborated in high-fat diet/streptozotocin- and methionine-choline–deficient mice. Systemically administered EVs predominantly accumulated in the liver and improved peripheral nerve structure and function, with benefits supported by glycemia-controlled or glycemia-adjusted analyses rather than being fully explained by systemic glycemic changes. EV treatment was associated with reduced circulating injury markers, attenuated spinal inflammatory responses, and improved endothelial junction integrity. Mechanistically, EV-encapsulated miR-24-3p repressed hepatic CD74, coinciding with reduced MHC II/NF-κB activity in macrophages. Hepatic CD74 overexpression promoted systemic inflammation and peripheral nerve injury, whereas pharmacologic NF-κB inhibition recapitulated EV-associated benefits. Together, these data define a liver-to-nerve causal axis and support EV-mediated restraint of hepatic CD74–NF-κB signaling as a cross-organ strategy for DPN repair.

papers.title: The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps
papers.abstract: Overexploitation of wildlife is one of the greatest global drivers of biodiversity loss. Yet, despite this well-established risk, data on extraction and trade are both incomplete and highly fragmented. The IPBES Global analysis estimated 50,000 species to be in trade, yet our review of wildlife trade monitoring programs found at least double that, at 107,356 species in use and trade globally. This included up to 47,685 animal species, covering 42% of all described vertebrate species. Most countries lack any systematic data on trade for species not listed in Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), with the exception of the US-specific dataset Law Enforcement Management Information System, which frequently had higher diversity of species in trade than global databases. This highlights the importance of national monitoring efforts and the need for standardized collation of wildlife trade data beyond CITES-listed species. Without these changes, global indicators on trade meant to guide sustainability and conservation will continue to focus on less than 2% of traded species.
papers.titleZh: 數據缺口掩蓋了全球野生動物貿易的真實規模

papers.title: ANME-2a perform methane oxidation in brackish coastal sediments via multiple pathways
papers.abstract: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Typically, a large fraction of methane formed in coastal sediments is removed via anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM). Here, we demonstrate the potential for a range of AOM pathways in brackish coastal sediments by ANME-2a archaea. At our study site, geochemical profiles indicate that AOM is primarily restricted to a shallow, metal oxide–rich sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ). ANME-2a were the sole methanotrophs detected, and metatranscriptomics showed the highest expression levels of the ANME-2a genes in the SMTZ. AOM activity was observed in sediment incubations with various electron acceptors, including sulfate, metal oxides, and the organic matter analog graphene oxide. Highest potential rates were observed in sediments from below the SMTZ, pointing toward fast stimulation of the deeper methanotrophic community when alleviating the electron acceptor limitation. The variety of AOM pathways and persistence of methanotrophs below the SMTZ likely contribute to the resilience of the microbial methane filter in brackish coastal sediments.
papers.titleZh: ANME-2a 在鹹淡海岸沉積物中透過多種途徑氧化甲烷
papers.summaryZh: 甲烷是強效溫室氣體，通常在海岸沉積物中形成的大量甲烷會經由厭氧甲烷氧化 AOM 移除。本研究在鹹淡海岸沉積物中展示 ANME-2a 古菌具有多種 AOM 途徑的潛力。在研究樣點，地球化學剖面顯示 AOM 主要侷限於淺層、富含金屬氧化物的硫酸鹽-甲烷轉換帶 SMTZ。ANME-2a 是檢測到的唯一甲烷營養菌，轉錄體學顯示 ANME-2a 基因在 SMTZ 的表現量最高。沉積物培養顯示在硫酸鹽、金屬氧化物以及有機物類似物氧化石墨烯等不同電子受體下均可觀察到 AOM 活性。來自 SMTZ 下方沉積物的潛在速率最高，顯示解除電子受體限制時深層甲烷營養群落可快速被刺激。AOM 途徑的多樣性與 SMTZ 下方甲烷營養菌的持續存在，可能有助於鹹淡海岸沉積物中微生物甲烷過濾器的韌性。

papers.title: Elevated CO2 mitigated warming-enhanced carbon loss from northern peatland
papers.abstract: Peatlands store one-third of the global soil carbon (C) on only ∼3% of Earth’s land surface but risk becoming C sources to accelerate climate change due to warming-induced C loss. Elevated CO 2 (eCO 2 ) may mitigate this loss by boosting plant C uptake. However, how eCO 2 and climate warming interact to influence peatland C dynamics remains unclear. Here, we investigated peatland C fate at five warming levels (+0°, +2.25°, +4.5°, +6.75°, and + 9°C), each under ambient CO 2 (aCO 2 ) and eCO 2 (+500 parts per million), by model-guided synthesis of 18 measured variables for each of the 10 treatments from an experiment. Our results showed that the peatland C loss increased with warming at a rate of 62.6 g C m −2 year −1 °C −1 , reaching 476.5 ± 104.7 g C m −2 year −1 at +9°C under aCO 2 , primarily because of increased Sphagnum mortality and accelerated decomposition. eCO 2 reduced the loss rate to 17.3 g C m −2 year −1 °C −1 , nearly halving the C loss at +9°C (269.4 ± 80.5 g C m −2 year −1 ), mainly due to enhanced tree and shrub growth. Methane emissions increased with warming, similarly under aCO 2 and eCO 2 . Our findings suggest that northern peatlands likely become major C sources under climate warming, although rising atmospheric CO 2 concentration may partially slow down the C loss. Climate-driven shifts in plant community structure, rather than peat decomposition alone, play a critical role in regulating peatland C fate and may threaten the stability of peatland ecosystem functions and services in the future.

papers.title: Oxygen-dependent constraint of glycolysis through the mitochondrial electron transport chain
papers.abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are constitutively active in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cells. Here, we investigated whether these cells could still respond to hypoxia independently of canonical HIF activation. We found that hypoxia provokes a NADH reductive stress that attenuates lactate release when the supply of extracellular pyruvate becomes limited, a response that was restored by the ectopic expression of the cytosolic and mitochondria-targeted NADH oxidase ( Lb NOX). Suppression of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mtETC) alone is sufficient to attenuate glycolytic flux when extracellular pyruvate is limited, a situation consistent with metabolomic data from human ccRCCs. Furthermore, this response can be mimicked by pharmacological or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) activity and restored by the mitochondrial-targeted alternative oxidase (AOX). Therefore, our data suggest that cells can respond to low oxygen tension through a mitochondrial-dependent elevation of NADH/NAD + , resulting in the suppression of glycolysis when pyruvate availability is compromised.

papers.title: GPR183 senses 7α,25-OHC to drive Treg differentiation and tumor immune evasion via AXL-JAK2-STAT5 signaling
papers.abstract: Regulatory T cell (T reg ) accumulation within the tumor microenvironment is a major contributor to immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance. However, the metabolic signals orchestrating T reg lineage commitment remain poorly defined. We identify that the oxysterol 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), produced by Vimentin + stromal cells, acts through GPR183 to promote T reg differentiation and suppressive identity. In patients with gastric cancer (GC), GPR183 + T reg infiltration correlates with advanced disease and poor survival. In syngeneic tumor models, conditional GPR183 deletion, specifically in CD4 + T cells or T reg cells, demonstrates its cell-intrinsic requirement for high-cholesterol-diet–induced T reg expansion and tumor growth, thereby abrogating immune evasion and restoring CD8 + T cell effector function. Mechanistically, 7α,25-OHC–GPR183 signaling activates the AXL-JAK2-STAT5 pathway to reinforce Foxp3 expression. Last, GPR183 antagonism modestly enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy in a model-dependent manner and prevents therapy-induced T reg expansion. These findings identify the 7α,25-OHC–GPR183–AXL axis as a potential metabolic checkpoint linking cholesterol metabolism to immune suppression, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to enhance antitumor immunity.

papers.title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions
papers.abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure—with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions—supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.

papers.title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian
papers.abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.

papers.title: A dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle delivery system for precision phage therapy against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
papers.abstract: The escalating crisis of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among Gram-negative bacteria, demands innovative therapeutic strategies. Here, we present a dual-targeting lipid nanoparticle-chimeric phage (AbLCP) system engineered to combat multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. Our design integrates a genetically modified M13 phage displaying anti–lipopolysaccharide (LPS) antibodies with polymyxin B conjugation, which is further encapsulated within anti-LPS antibody–functionalized lipid nanoparticles. This system overcomes the fundamental limitations of conventional phage therapy, enabling efficient cellular internalization, endosomal escape, and potent intracellular bactericidal activity. In murine models of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, AbLCP achieved superior bacterial clearance and up to 10 3 -fold reduction in bacterial burden at a 10 3 -fold lower effective dose than free polymyxin B, with 67-fold selective accumulation at infection sites, and attenuated systemic inflammation and preservation of gut microbiota. Mechanistically, AbLCP neutralized LPS to suppress inflammation and induced a lethal bacterial stress response. This work establishes a transformative nanophage platform that merges synthetic biology with nanomedicine, offering a promising strategy against MDR bacterial infections.

papers.title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication
papers.abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform—Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

papers.title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
papers.abstract: Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plus FGF21 -encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of Lactobacillus plantarum -derived extracellular vesicles ( L. plantarum EVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment with L. plantarum EVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.

papers.title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
papers.abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.

papers.summaryZh: 本文為綜述，聚焦於細胞間粒線體轉移作為治療策略的潛力。作者指出細胞具有內在的修復性溝通，可交換生物活性分子甚至整個細胞器，並強調粒線體轉移能恢復受損細胞的生物能量能力、減緩氧化壓力並挽救代謝功能。文中提到粒線體功能缺陷與多種病理相關，並說明粒線體轉移旨在將功能性粒線體遞送至受傷細胞以重建代謝能力。作者也指出目前臨床轉譯面臨器官輸送不足與轉移動態控制有限等障礙，並回顧近期透過提升供受體連接性、增加粒線體可用性與調控轉移機制等生物技術發展。綜述最後整理粒線體轉移生物工程的最新進展、潛在治療應用，以及需解決以實現臨床應用的關鍵挑戰。
